excerpt:
Pure-Python library for TeX/LaTeX processing. Parses TeX input and produces PDF,
SVG, and DVI output. No external TeX installation required — Computer Modern
fonts and hyphenation patterns are bundled.
classification_basis: MT031 mixed-unit treatment: the core claim (pure-Python TeX/LaTeX processing, PDF/SVG/DVI output, no external TeX install needed, bundled Computer Modern fonts) is real and verified. The trailing 'and hyphenation patterns are bundled' clause is FALSE as of this checkout: src/aspose_tex/data/hyphenation/ contains only a .gitkeep placeholder, data/README.md itself says US-English patterns 'will be added', and the \patterns/\hyphenation primitives (_engine/expansion.py) are registered no-ops that parse and discard their argument. Merged with the false sub-claim dropped, not carried forward.

verification.evidence_note: data/README.md's own hyphenation/ section: 'Holds language-specific hyphenation pattern files. US-English hyphenation patterns (public domain) will be added. ... Empty at this stage.' Corroborated by a direct directory listing (hyphenation/ contains only .gitkeep) and by _engine/expansion.py:382 ('if name in ("patterns", "hyphenation"): self._consume_balanced_text_discard(name)' — a documented no-op). Fonts-bundled half corroborated separately: src/aspose_tex/data/fonts/ contains 55 real .pfb and 76 real .tfm files.

SVG output is self-contained — glyph outlines are extracted from the bundled
Computer Modern PFB fonts and embedded as `<path>` elements, so no external
fonts are required by the SVG viewer.

excerpt:
`TeXJob.messages` returns a copy of the messages collected during the most
recent run. `\message` and `\write 16` append plain-text messages; `\errmessage`
appends messages with a leading `! ` prefix; `\write -1` logs only.
classification_basis: A real, distinct, currently-functional capability fact (job-level diagnostics collection) recovered into Key Capabilities.

verification.evidence_note: io_primitives.py's exec_message/exec_write/exec_errmessage implement exactly this behavior; TeXJob.messages (presentation/__init__.py) returns list(self._messages), a defensive copy.
